title: Dissolving sodium chloride
caption: ΔsolH = −ΔlattH(formation) + ΔhydH(Na⁺) + ΔhydH(Cl⁻) = +787 − 406 − 364 = +17 kJ mol⁻¹ with these values (data books give about +4). Separating the lattice costs almost exactly what hydrating the ions returns, so NaCl dissolves with a small enthalpy change, driven by entropy.
alt: Enthalpy diagram: NaCl(s) low; up 787 to the gaseous ions; down 406 and 364 for hydration to Na⁺(aq) + Cl⁻(aq), just above NaCl(s).
description: Up +787 kJ mol⁻¹ to Na⁺(g) + Cl⁻(g): breaking up the lattice.
Down −364 kJ mol⁻¹: hydrating Cl⁻, ending 17 kJ mol⁻¹ above the start.
